And now I say it again. Can't guard me."

Again, that was in the heat of battle on Monday. In the calm of a midweek press conference out at The Star, Cowboys reporters asked Lamb about that clip, which made the rounds on social media.

Lamb explained why, exactly, no one on the planet can guard him: "I think my ability to line up anywhere in the offense and run any route on the route tree. I feel like I can beat anybody in front of me. I'm gonna stand on that."

Lamb also noted that when the Cowboys offense is rolling–which has been the case only sporadically this season it is generally difficult to guard.

He noted: "It's almost like it is inevitable because regardless what coverage you put on it, there is nothing blanketing it. You have an option, you have an answer for every coverage. I feel like in that realm, as an offensive player, you like it because it is like the mercy is in your court."

Cowboys Winless vs. Arizona in WR's Career

If there is a time for some humility from Lamb, though, it will be this week entering Sunday's Week 8 game against the Cardinals . In four tries during his NFL career, Lamb has gone 0-4 against Arizona.

He noted that the Cowboys have taken them too lightly in the past, and that the Cardinals have been amped up for the matchup from the get go. "We've been very relaxed and they've punched us in the mouth every single time," Lamb said.

articles.title: UConn Women's Basketball: When Are Huskies Alums Playing in WNBA Game 7?
articles.summary: The Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream will meet on Saturday night.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream defeated the Golden State Valkyries (80-69) in Game 6 of the WNBA Finals on Thursday afternoon, forcing a Game 7 that is set for Saturday night at 8 p.m. ET in Golden State.

This will be the first-ever Game 7 in WNBA Finals history, as the league just adopted a best-of-seven championship series in 2025.

Several former UConn Huskies women's basketball alums will be representing Golden State in its quest to win the first title in franchise history:

Kaitlyn Chen, Tiffany Hayes, Kiah Stokes and Gabby Williams all play for Golden State. This is just the second year that the franchise has existed.

Chen played three years of college basketball at Princeton before transferring to UConn for her senior year in 2024-25. With the Huskies, she played and started 40 games, averaging 6.9 ppg and 3.4 assists. She helped the Huskies win the national title alongside Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd and was drafted No. 30 overall in the 2025 WNBA Draft.

She was the Ivy League Player of the Year in 2022-23 at Princeton. She played just five minutes in the Game 6 loss. She averaged 7.2 ppg in the regular season.

Williams, the most decorated former Huskies star on the Valkyries, is also an incredibly accomplished WNBA player. She had 26 points, three rebounds and three steals on Thursday.

A four-year standout for the Huskies, Williams crossed over with legendary forward Breanna Stewart for two of UConn's four straight national titles (2015 and 2016). She started 85 games in Storrs, getting named Defensive Player of the Year in 2017. She was also a two-time Associated Press All-American and a two-time All-AAC selection. She averaged 10.6 ppg for her career and was the No. 4 overall pick in the 2018 WNBA Draft (Chicago Sky).

She's also represented France on the international stage, leading the French to the Olympic silver medal in 2024 and a second-place finish at this year's FIBA World Cup.

Hayes scored 15 points in 28 minutes on Thursday. She won two national titles at UConn in 2008-09 and 2009-10. She played in 154 games with the Huskies, averaging 11.7 ppg for her career. An All-American in her senior year, she was also a three-time All-Big East selection who was drafted No. 14 overall in the 2012 WNBA Draft. Ironically, she was taken by the Dream and spent 10 years there before also playing with Las Vegas, Connecticut and Golden State.

Another starter for Golden State, she had zero points in 20 minutes on Thursday. She averaged 3.6 ppg and 5.8 rebounds a game this season.

A three-time national champion at UConn, she also had crossover with Stewart and Williams. She averaged 4.5 ppg for her career and was the 2014-15 AAC Defensive Player of the Year. She was taken No. 11 overall in 2015 by the New York Liberty.

articles.title: Jerry Jones once explained why Donald Trump was ‘problematic’ for the NFL
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones once admitted that Donald Trump’s involvement in the NFL’s national anthem debate was damaging to the league, describing the...
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones once admitted that Donald Trump's involvement in the NFL's national anthem debate was damaging to the league, describing the president's interest as "problematic".

Jones made the comments in 2018, when the NFL was attempting to resolve the controversy surrounding players kneeling during the national anthem to protest racial injustice.

The debate had become a major talking point after Trump publicly criticised players who protested and urged the league to punish those who refused to stand.

Jerry Jones admitted Donald Trump's comments were problematic for the NFL

Speaking at the Cowboys' training camp in California, Jones acknowledged that Trump's comments were creating difficulties for NFL owners.

"His interest in what we're doing is problematic from my chair, and I would say in general the owners' chair," Jones said.

He also admitted that owners wanted the controversy to end, adding: "It's unprecedented if you really think about it. Yes I would like — everybody would like — for it to go away."

Jones was not the only NFL owner to express concerns. Cincinnati Bengals owner Mike Brown also suggested that Trump's comments had worked against the league, claiming the debate had made people view the NFL unfavourably.

However, Jones maintained that the Cowboys would expect their players to stand during the national anthem, making the team's position clear despite the wider disagreement.

"It did not impact our position," he said. "Our position is very clear in that you should stand."

The comments came amid wider tensions between the NFL and its players' association over the league's proposed anthem policy. The NFLPA had argued that the policy infringed on players' rights, while discussions between the two sides continued.

The controversy also raised concerns among sponsors and team owners, particularly as reports suggested NFL television ratings had declined during the previous season.

Jones had owned the Cowboys since 1989, and the franchise's commercial success meant that any damage to the league's popularity was a significant concern.

His comments offered a glimpse into the difficult position NFL owners faced as Trump's criticism brought the national anthem debate back into the spotlight.

articles.title: Carolina Panthers 19-27 Green Bay Packers: Jordan Love throws three touchdown passes in vital win
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers beat the Carolina Panthers 27-19 at Lambeau Field; Jordan Love threw three touchdowns and Christian Watson returned to the game after going to the hospital; watch the 2026 NFL season live on Sky Sports, including every minute of the playoffs
articles.body:
Love went 30 of 41 for 288 yards with touchdown passes to Tucker Kraft, Matthew Golden and Jacobs plus an interception. Although Jacobs rushed for only 39 yards on 21 carries against the NFL's lowest-ranked run defense, he scored on a 4-yard catch and 1-yard run.

That was more than enough for the Packers on a night when they sacked Bryce Young six times. Green Bay hasn't allowed any of its last five opponents to exceed 20 points.

"This defense is really special," safety Javon Bullard said.

Trailing 27-10 in the third quarter, Carolina cut Green Bay's lead to 27-19 on Young's 26-yard touchdown pass to Jalen Coker on a fourth-and-three play with 5:37 remaining. Young's ensuing 2-point conversion pass was incomplete.

"Late in the game, it wasn't good enough," Love said. "We weren't able to finish the way we wanted. That's something we've got to improve on, clean up as an offense and be better there."

The Panthers (3-4) got the ball back at their own 45 before losing the ball on downs at midfield with 2:41 remaining. Carolina got one last chance from its own 20 with 22 seconds and no timeouts remaining, but Dani Dennis-Sutton's sack essentially ended any comeback hopes.

Young went 23 of 41 for 209 yards with one touchdown and one interception. Carolina's Chuba Hubbard had 22 carries for 81 yards and a touchdown and seven catches for 38 yards.

Green Bay's Christian Watson returned to the game after hurting his chest while making a 53-yard catch in the second quarter, causing him to be taken to the hospital. Carolina cornerback Will Lee hurt his hamstring while diving to make a tackle on the same play, and he got carted into the locker room.

Watson said he got clearance to return to the game after a CT scan didn't show any internal bleeding. Watson did say he broke a rib on the play.

"I felt like I was watching 'WWE Smackdown vs. Raw' or something, seeing the cameras on me when I was coming out of the ambulance," said Watson, who caught eight passes for 113 yards. "That was a little crazy. It was a surreal experience, no doubt."

After fumbling the opening kickoff to set up a Carolina field goal and going three-and-out on their first series, the Packers (5-3) scored touchdowns on three of their next four possessions to take command.

Love threw a 12-yard touchdown pass across the middle to Kraft on a third-and-8 play to put Green Bay ahead 6-3, as struggling rookie Trey Smack's extra-point attempt bounced off the left upright.

Watson's 53-yard catch set up a Jacobs touchdown run that put Green Bay ahead for good, 13-10 early in the second quarter. One play after dropping a potential touchdown pass, Golden caught a 24-yarder in the left corner of the end zone on third-and-13 to make it 20-10.

Carolina got the ball to start the second half, but Chris McClellan and Evan Williams stopped Hubbard a yard short on fourth-and-two from midfield. On Green Bay's ensuing drive, Love found Jacobs to extend the lead to 27-10.

Green Bay led 27-13 and had the ball on Carolina's 28 in the opening minute of the fourth quarter when Love threw a pass to Golden that Zakee Wheatley intercepted in the end zone.

That turnover sparked Carolina's comeback attempt, but the Panthers ultimately couldn't break through against Green Bay's defense.

"I said at the beginning of the year, and I still feel this way: I think the sky is the limit for this defense," Packers linebacker Isaiah McDuffie said.

The Packers - while 5-3 - still sit bottom of the NFC North, the NFL's strongest division, while the Panthers remain atop the NFC South even with a negative record on the season.

articles.title: Packers' Jacobs Says TD Celebration that Drew Criticism was Modeled After a Gospel Song
articles.summary: GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs says he was paying homage to a gospel song rather than making light of his recent arrest when he briefly had his hands behind his back while celebrating a touchdown Thursday night.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs says he was paying homage to a gospel song rather than making light of his recent arrest when he briefly had his hands behind his back while celebrating a touchdown Thursday night.

This was Jacobs' second game of the season after coming off the commissioner's exempt list. He was placed on that list after charges were filed against him in August stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend during which she said he threw her to the ground.

Jacobs pleaded no contest last month to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property.

Jacobs had just scored on a 1-yard run in the second quarter of the Packers' 27-19 victory over the Carolina Panthers when he put his hands behind his back for a moment while accepting congratulations from teammates. The video garnered plenty of attention on social media as some who watched on television believed Jacobs was simulating getting handcuffed.

Jacobs said he instead was modeling his celebration after a gospel song called "Break Every Chain."

"The guys did it with me," Jacobs said. "I didn't think it was going to be a thing that can be perceived a certain type of way. But it's 2026, and it is what it is."

Jacobs said he had spoken with Savion Williams and other receivers before making his season debut, and they came up with the idea that he would do a celebration thanking God after his first touchdown of the season. That celebration happened Sunday, as he went to his knees and raised his arms aloft after scoring in a 20-17 loss at Detroit.

They also had planned this "Break Every Chain" celebration after his second touchdown of the season. When Jacobs was asked about putting his hands behind his back as part of the celebration, he noted that the telecast only showed a brief portion of what he did.

"It was more to it than that," Jacobs said. "They stopped showing the celebration after that. Like I said, it is what it is."

Jacobs hadn't been able to play or practice while he was on the commissioner's exempt list. He was removed from that list last week, enabling him to play again even though the NFLs investigation of him remains ongoing.

articles.title: The Top 5 Realistic Trade Deadline Targets for the Cleveland Browns
articles.summary: The 5-2 Cleveland Browns enter the NFL trade deadline in rare territory: Their record is good enough that they could justify being buyers.
articles.body:
The 5-2 Cleveland Browns enter the NFL trade deadline in rare territory: Their record is good enough that they could justify being buyers.

The beginning of the season was marked with rumors and buzz of the Browns offloading Jerry Jeudy or a quarterback in the hunt for more draft capital.

Instead, a hot start and some notable needs on the roster have them in a justifiable position to push some chips to the middle of the table.

That being said, it's unlikely the Browns will go all-in on the biggest names. They are still a young team and Andrew Berry has built it through a hot streak in the draft lately.

Considering the Browns' cap space, roster and situation, we'll rank the team's top five most realistic trade targets ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.

5. CB Amik Robertson, Washington Commanders

Possible Impact: Myles Harden has been inconsistent throughout the season thus far. He'd immediately be fighting for his job if Amik Robertson came to Cleveland. The veteran's inside-out versatility could see him take Harden's job or back up Tyson Campbell and Denzel Ward.

Projected Cost: Late Day 3 pick or Day 3 pick swap

Why It Could Happen: The Browns' depth at cornerback is questionable. It's an underrated issue that could rear its head as the playoff chase gets tighter. Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell have each had their own issues with injuries throughout their careers.

Harden has also struggled in the slot so Robertson would be an appropriate solution to two different problems.

Why It Won't: The Commanders are in position to sell at 1-4-1, but their cornerback room has been particularly dreadful. The secondary is giving up a 105.0 passer rating . Robertson has been better than most of their options so they might not be willing to part with him.

From the Browns' perspective, the need at cornerback might not be severe enough to warrant a move.

4. Edge Khalil Mack, Los Angeles Chargers

Possible Impact: Mack would immediately become the most experienced member of the young Browns defensive line. He has lost a step at 35 years old, but he's a nuanced pass-rusher who is still getting to the quarterback.

Why It Could Happen: The Chargers are 0-6 heading into Week 8. That's a pretty good reason to ship off a 35-year-old veteran who no longer holds long-term value.

Mack has the kind of juice in the pass rush that the group needs to bolster the outside rotation.

Why It Won't: Some of the younger pass-rushers could end up being part of the long-term solution in Cleveland. Mack cannot. If Andrew Berry is looking for anything more than a half-season rental, then Mack is not the answer.

The Chargers may also prefer to send Mack elsewhere. He's been with the franchise for five seasons and if he prefers to go to a more proven contender, they may be willing to accommodate.

3. TE Charlie Kolar, Los Angeles Chargers

Possible Impact: A blocking tight end would open up the Browns' offense to include more 12 personnel usage. Kolar is a strong blocker with ties to Todd Monken from his Ravens days.

Projected Cost: 2027 fifth-round pick or Day 3 pick swap

Why It Could Happen: The Chargers are 0-6 and in a position to be selling off assets. Kolar would be a perfect fit as a secondary tight end behind Harold Fannin.

Kolar should be relatively cheap on the trade market. It's a perfectly justifiable swing to tip the odds in the Browns' favor moving forward without going all-in on a big name.

Why It Won't: The Chargers signed Kolar to a three-year contract this offseason. So while it wouldn't cost the Browns much draft capital to take him on, they would be taking on the rest of that contract.

Monken might also be comfortable with his personnel usage at this point. The Cleveland offense is far from prolific, but it's doing just enough to win games so Kolar could be seen as unnecessary.

Top 10 Realistic Trade Deadline Targets for the Buffalo Bills

2. Edge Jermaine Johnson II, Tennessee Titans

Possible Impact: The Browns just got a firsthand look at what Jermaine Johnson can offer the defense. He beat the Cleveland front for five total pressures, per Sports Info Solutions .

Johnson is a gritty, physical edge player who plays the run well and wins with power as a pass-rusher. He would give the Browns an edge-rusher opposite Jared Verse who would defend the run and take advantage of one-on-one blocking.

Why It Could Happen: The Browns have a strong pass-rush, but finding another edge who could join the rotation would potentially take them to another level. The playoffs are usually full of teams with deep pass-rushing rotations.

The current coaching staff and front office don't really have connections to Johnson, but they just watched him play and his physicality would match up with what the Browns have.

Why It Won't: The Titans just traded away Jeffery Simmons and received two first-round picks in the deal. They aren't exactly going to be desperate to offload another defensive lineman, especially one who as is young and productive as Johnson.

The fit isn't perfect either. Johnson fits in with the Browns' current personnel on the edge, but a more speed-oriented rusher with bend would be a better addition.

Possible Impact: The 29-year-old edge-rusher is just one year removed from a 12-sack campaign with the Cardinals. He has two for the season thus far and would ostensibly increase that total on a defensive line that has been as disruptive as the Browns have been.

Why It Could Happen: Sweat is the exact stylistic fit the Browns need to bookend with Verse. He's a faster pass-rusher who can still bend as he plays out his age-29 season.

The Cardinals are 2-5 and Sweat came to Arizona as part of the Jonathan Gannon era. The former Eagles defensive coordinator is no longer in charge so Sweat might not be part of their plans.

Why It Won't: It has to be acknowledged that Sweat is coming off a knee injury that landed him on the PUP list at the beginning of the season. He did not look like himself over the first few weeks of the season.

However, he's since put up two sacks and 10 pressures over the last four games. That would make him one of the most productive edge-rushers on the Browns roster right now and the injury could help the team acquire him for cheaper.

articles.title: The Top 10 Realistic Trade Deadline Targets for the Buffalo Bills
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills are on the verge of returning from their bye week, but there will be precious little time to evaluate the roster before the NFL trade deadline hits on Nov. 10.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills are on the verge of returning from their bye week, but there will be precious little time to evaluate the roster before the NFL trade deadline hits on Nov. 10.

That deadline falls just hours after the Bills play the Minnesota Vikings on Monday Night Football to wrap up Week 9, leaving them with only that prime-time clash and this weekend's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens to finalize their strategy.

As the market heats up, here are 10 candidates who could realistically find themselves employed in Western New York before Week 10 arrives.

Contract information courtesy of Spotrac .

10. Washington Commanders CB Rasul Douglas

The Profile: The 31-year-old has 22 career interceptions and 96 starts dating back a decade. He's been on the field for 67 percent of Washington's defensive snaps this season, ranking 22nd among 73 qualified corners with a 67.0 grade at Pro Football Focus .

The Fit: Bills general manager Brandon Beane acquired Douglas at the 2023 deadline, and it would make sense to inquire about him again with Washington's season in the gutter. Douglas is on a cheap one-year deal in Washington, and he'd arguably provide an upgrade over Maxwell Hairston and rookie Davison Igbinosun as a veteran playmaker.

The Predicted Cost: A 2027 seventh-round draft pick.

The Potential Obstacle: Igbinosun may be a liability, but he's emerging. Acquiring another cornerback now could come across as an admission from Beane that he erred in selecting Hairston in the first round in 2025 and Igbinosun in Round 2 one year later.

The Profile: The 28-year-old has compiled more than 400 tackles over the course of an eight-year career with three teams. He's started all seven games this season in Arizona, where he continues to flash versatility and reliability but is far from spectacular.

The Fit: He'd bring plenty of physicality to Buffalo while improving the defense's ability to cover tight ends. Wilson isn't a star, but he'd immediately bolster a bland linebacker group that is consistently vulnerable one way or the other. He'd cost the Bills less than $2 million before his contract expires this spring.

The Predicted Cost: A 2027 sixth-round draft pick.

The Potential Obstacle: Beane used Day 2 draft picks on Terrel Bernard and Dorian Williams just a few years ago, and both should in theory be in their primes.

The Profile: The 29-year-old—he turns 30 three days after the deadline—recorded at least 100 tackles in each of his first three seasons as a regular starter (2022–2024). He's somewhat of a journeyman, but he brings extensive starting experience. This season, the 2019 third-round pick has a top-20 pass-rushing grade among qualified off-ball linebackers at PFF.

The Fit: Barton would have a chance to pair with Bernard as a stuffer in run defense, or even replace him next to Williams on obvious passing downs. At the very least, he'd bring some much-needed oomph and variation to that position of need.

The Potential Obstacle: Not only would Barton cost $3.6 million the rest of this season, but the Bills would owe him another $7 million in 2027.

The Profile: The 2021 third-round pick is a versatile, high-IQ defensive back who shined in his debut season with the Chargers. The 27-year-old hasn't been as effective since and missed some time in September but ranks 18th among qualified safeties with a PFF grade of 73.5.

The Fit: Molden could offer an upgrade over C.J. Gardner-Johnson as a disciplined deep safety who can also play in the box and handle slot duties. A deadline acquisition would cost Buffalo approximately $3.3 million against the cap for the remainder of this season.

The Predicted Cost: A 2027 fifth-round draft pick.

The Potential Obstacle: This isn't a rental—Buffalo would be on the hook for another $5.3 million next year—and the Bills already paid CJGJ to pair with the young Cole Bishop. The Chargers might also drive a hard bargain considering Molden's age and contract.

The Profile: The 27-year-old intercepted six passes in a Pro Bowl rookie season in 2022 and remained a key contributor over the course of his four-year rookie contract in Seattle. He signed a one-year, $12 million deal with the Eagles in the 2026 offseason and currently ranks 48th among 114 qualified corners with a 63.1 PFF grade.

The Fit: Woolen brings sheer size, speed and talent to the table and has the scheme versatility to blend in quickly. He'd likely push to be the No. 2 corner immediately.

The Predicted Cost: A 2027 third-round draft pick.

The Potential Obstacle: The Eagles might see him as part of their future. Even if they don't, Buffalo could face significant competition for a 27-year-old rental corner who would cost his new team less than $1 million for the remainder of the season and is scheduled to become a free agent in 2027.

5. Los Angeles Chargers CB Donte Jackson

The Profile: The 30-year-old—he turns 31 two days before the deadline—has 23 interceptions and 109 starts over the course of a nine-year career to date. Among cornerbacks who started at least six games in 2025, he ranked first with an opposing passer rating of 48.6 while intercepting four passes.

The Fit: You're getting one of the most experienced and accomplished cover guys in the league for a Super Bowl run. Jim Leonhard has shown a strong preference for zone coverage this season, and Jackson would be in a position to excel there while helping a young defense cut down on communication issues. All at a cost of just $3.3 million for the remainder of 2026, which is a walk year for Jackson.

The Potential Obstacle: If Jackson is available, he'll be in very high demand. It's also not ideal that he's currently recovering from a hamstring injury.

The Profile: The 30-year-old is an eight-time Pro Bowler who recorded a combined 284 tackles the last two seasons and is on pace for yet another triple-digit-tackle campaign in 2026. He may be slightly beyond his prime, but Baker already has a career-best 3.5 sacks despite a mediocre overall PFF grade of 54.8 thus far this year.

The Fit: While he wouldn't really be a one-for-one replacement for Gardner-Johnson, Baker would provide an upgrade over the still-green Bishop inside the box and could be a massive game-changer for the entire defense. His very presence would help the rest of a struggling secondary and linebacker corps excel.

The Predicted Cost: A 2027 fourth-round draft pick.

The Potential Obstacle: The cap-strapped Bills would either have to convince Arizona to pay a portion of Baker's remaining 2026 salary or restructure other contracts to accommodate him. Asking the Cardinals to cover salary could mean adding draft capital to the deal. Baker is also under contract through 2027, when he is scheduled to earn approximately $17.8 million in salary and bonuses, none of it guaranteed, giving Beane another financial consideration beyond this season.

The Profile: The 28-year-old has spent his entire eight-year career in Tennessee, where he hit a groove with five interceptions in 2024. He followed that up with a down year in 2025 but already has two picks and is PFF's ninth-highest-graded safety thus far in 2026.

The Fit: He's got the versatility and experience the Bills could use both inside and outside of the box. You almost never have to take him off the field, lessening the burden on Gardner-Johnson and Bishop.

The Potential Obstacle: The $4.9 million 2026 price tag is manageable, but that'll shoot up above $10 million as Hooker hits 29 in 2027. The Titans also just traded Jeffery Simmons and might prefer to stop short of a fire sale, considering that they signed Hooker to an extension only a year ago.

The Profile: The 28-year-old has intercepted eight passes since the start of 2024, establishing himself as one of the most versatile and reliable free safeties in the league. He hasn't missed a start since his 2021 rookie season in Minnesota.

The Fit: Bynum would provide an immediate upgrade at the position, allowing the team to rely less on both Gardner-Johnson and Bishop. He'd also bring tremendous energy to the defense.

The Potential Obstacle: There's a strong chance the Colts still see Bynum as part of their future and refuse to include him as part of their current fire sale unless the return is off the charts. And while his $5.8 million cost for 2026 would be doable with some maneuvering, the Bills would be looking at a $14 million price tag next season.

The Profile: The 29-year-old two-time Pro Bowler has been on the field for more than 95 percent of Philadelphia's defensive snaps since the start of 2024. That year, Baun was a legitimate Defensive Player of the Year candidate. This year, his PFF grade of 79.1 ranks fifth among qualified players at his position.

The Fit: Baun played under Jim Leonhard at Wisconsin. As an incredibly productive, versatile defender who can play off-ball or rush the passer, he'd be the ultimate new chess piece for Leonhard without rendering any of the current starters useless.

The Predicted Cost: A 2027 second-round draft pick.

The Potential Obstacle: If the Eagles are willing to trade Baun, he'll have a lot of suitors considering the acquiring team would be on the hook for less than $700,000 for the remainder of 2026—even with $17 million in scheduled compensation looming in 2027. The price could easily exceed my prediction above via a bidding war.

articles.title: Buyer, Seller, or Stand Pat? Predicting Every NFL Team's Trade Deadline Strategy
articles.summary: The NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline is fast approaching, leaving front offices little time to decide whether to buy, sell, or stand pat.
articles.body:
The NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline is fast approaching, leaving front offices little time to decide whether to buy, sell, or stand pat.

With October football wrapping up, let's nail down every team's likely approach to the deadline.

They're a prime contender as is, but the defensive back seven absolutely needs a boost for a team that remains flawed despite entering Week 8 as the Super Bowl favorite at FanDuel .

The rebuild hasn't left them with much to sell off, but now could be a good time to get a king's ransom from a desperate contender for expensive 31-year-old Zach Sieler.

As with Buffalo, the core is pretty locked in and they're tight for salary-cap space. They made their splashes in the offseason and likely shouldn't sacrifice any more significant draft capital.

This season is already a lost cause and it appears Aaron Glenn is a lame duck. Time to get something back for guys who won't likely be part of the next generation, like Geno Smith and Harrison Phillips.

It's becoming obvious that this team won't get over the top without another high-impact defender, ideally in the secondary. That said, they're in the worst cap shape in the league.

Like Baltimore, they have a desperate need for at least one more elite defensive player, if not a star back like Jonathan Taylor. The Bengals are right there following a 4-2 start, and they can't afford to miss the playoffs again. They need a home run.

They're hanging right now but are not a realistic Super Bowl contender. You don't want to break up a good thing, but sacrificing capital for a rental makes little sense either. Deshaun Watson would have been the real bait here, but that door has likely closed for now.

They're invested in Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy, so a reset is out of the question following a 5-2 start. But when you look at the receiving corps, this team has little choice but to keep gunning.

I don't think they're ready to fold, as doing so might spell the end of the C.J. Stroud era entirely. The Marvin Harrison Jr. acquisition might have been their primary splash, however.

This isn't a prediction, as the fire sale is well underway with DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson leaving town this month.

The Brian Thomas Jr. rumors have reached a fever pitch, but the first-place Jags will likely try to leverage Thomas and some draft capital to bolster their odds of making their first-ever Super Bowl trip.

This was confirmed with the Jeffery Simmons trade to Chicago. Now I'd fully expect veterans like Amani Hooker and Cody Barton to be available at discounted rates.

Insider: 'All Hell' to Break Loose at Deadline

There aren't a lot of obvious upgrade opportunities for a team that has been building this up deliberately. The only potential splash I see would be a deal for Saquon Barkley or Jonathan Taylor, which is unlikely.

It's an all-or-nothing situation at this point, and they're widely expected to pursue a standout receiver at the very least.

This team isn't a contender yet, so it makes little sense to sacrifice the future by paying premiums for short-term solutions. On the other end of the spectrum, you also don't want to sacrifice current talent before Fernando Mendoza takes over.

This season has gone down the drain, but the Chargers are largely stuck with their current core. While I doubt they're ready to blow it all up, moving on from a veteran defender like Khalil Mack, Derwin James, Donte Jackson or Elijah Molden could make sense.

The Cowboys are still favored to win the NFC East in what may be a make-or-break season for the head coach and the quarterback. In order to finally make waves in January, they likely need another high-impact defender. They have some cap space to work with, too.

You don't want to kill the momentum from a hot start by messing with this operation right now, and the reality is this is not a Super Bowl team yet anyway. It makes sense to sit this deadline out.

This isn't an easy call when you've been a perennial contender and are locked in with a franchise quarterback, but they've already indicated they're prepared to blow the rest of it up. Zack Baun, Saquon Barkley and Dallas Goedert are good "sell high" candidates right now.

With just one win under their belt entering Week 8, it's becoming clear this team doesn't have it. With a coaching change probably coming, dealing vets like Daron Payne, Stefon Diggs, Frankie Luvu and Dorance Armstrong would be prudent.

Mission accomplished with the Jeffery Simmons trade. The Bears are officially in it to win it.

What choice do they have now that Simmons is a Bear? The window is closing in Detroit, and there is cap space for a major defensive addition.

Money is a fair bit tighter here, and Green Bay is already down a 2027 first-round pick. The goal ahead of this deadline might simply be to shore up support for Jordan Love, potentially add a depth defensive lineman and hope they've got what it takes beyond that.

I don't think they want to mess with what they have right now, and there aren't many glaring soft spots on the roster. It's possible they chase Jonathan Taylor or Saquon Barkley, but a Minnesota team with little cap space is much more likely to add a depth piece in the offensive backfield and forge ahead.

They're in the thick of the wide-open NFC South race, so I get not selling. But the Falcons aren't a realistic Super Bowl contender and can't justify sacrificing the future for short-term rentals. They should focus on adding depth at cornerback or wide receiver.

Same idea as the Falcons. You can't sell when you're in first place, right? But what would be the point in buying big when it's unlikely to put you over the top? Besides, they rank 31st in the NFL in cap space .

It's now officially safe to say this isn't the year for the 2-5 Saints, who would be smart to get max returns for Cesar Ruiz and Alvin Kamara as the rebuild continues.

This old team is 4-12 in its last 16 games. Time to load up ahead of an inevitable rebuild, meaning guys like Vita Vea and Chris Godwin should be on the block.

You don't want to strip the offense of all of its parts before auditioning Carson Beck, but now is a great time to get something for Budda Baker as well as quarterback Jacoby Brissett. They'd be silly not to entertain offers for Josh Sweat, too.

They've already done a lot of buying, but that clearly wasn't enough. They don't have the draft capital or cap space to make massive waves, but I'd still expect them to add a veteran receiver in an all-or-nothing situation.

The core here is not young and the 49ers are a true top-end contender. With plenty of cap space, I wouldn't expect them to be done making deals following the acquisition of DeForest Buckner.

The Quenton Nelson move is already enough to reach "light buyer" level. I'm not sure they have more in them from that standpoint, but I wouldn't fault them for giving up some capital for an experienced edge.

articles.title: Re-Drafting 2026 NFL Draft Entering Week 8
articles.summary: The talent found within the 2026 NFL draft class had been downplayed during the process itself. It shouldn't have been then. In retrospect, it definitely shouldn't be now.
articles.body:
The talent found within the 2026 NFL draft class had been downplayed during the process itself. It shouldn't have been then. In retrospect, it definitely shouldn't be now.

Interestingly, five of the first 10 picks remained the same in this redraft, which indicates those teams were accurate in their assessments. Conversely, those individuals considered elite prospects have come to play. In fact, eight of the reworked top 11 include names called among the top-14 picks during April's event.

This specific class serves as a lesson for those who study the NFL draft. A class shouldn't be considered "down" simply because it lacks high-end talent at specific positions. Instead, look closely at what's available and how it can impact the league. From that perspective, the 2026 class has already proved successful entering Week 8.

With that said, some teams would have been in a better position today had they gone in a different direction when they were on the clock this past spring.

1. Las Vegas Raiders: QB Fernando Mendoza, Indiana

Fernando Mendoza has yet to start a game for the Las Vegas Raiders. There's no reason to change this selection since things have mostly gone according to plan for the organization.

Although, Mendoza's insertion to the lineup may happen sooner rather than later since Las Vegas lost its last four games with veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins at the helm.

Mendoza was the only quarterback worthy of first-round consideration this year. The reigning Heisman Trophy winner is the future of the Raiders offense. Nothing has indicated the team should have gone in another direction, particularly since he's yet to receive significant playing time.

Thus, this pick remains the same as everyone awaits the start of the Mendoza era in Sin City.

2. New York Jets: Edge David Bailey, Texas Tech

The best natural pass-rusher in the 2026 NFL draft class has transitioned well into the professional ranks.

From an on-field standpoint, David Bailey has been the league's best rookie regardless of position or draft status. This year's second overall draft pick leads all first-year players in sacks (5.5)—which is tied for fifth among all defenders—and total pressures (26) as the 2026 campaign starts to round its halfway point. The New York Jets found themselves in a draft position where they couldn't address quarterback after the Las Vegas Raiders made Fernando Mendoza the No. 1 overall pick. Instead, Gang Green found a cornerstone for the team's defense and should be thrilled with the initial return.

3. Arizona Cardinals: Edge Gabe Jacas, Illinois

The first major turn occurs with the third overall draft pick. At the time, the Arizona Cardinals' decision to select running back Jeremiyah Love felt like a luxury pick. Instead of going in the same direction, the organization addresses a premium position by selecting arguably the biggest surprise among this year's class.

Gabe Jacas slid to the back end of the second round before the New England Patriots chose him with the 55th overall pick. He's quickly asserted himself as a tenacious pass-rusher. His 21 pressures are second among rookies (behind David Bailey). From a holistic standpoint, Jacas actually led all first-year defenders in pass-rush win rate entering this past weekend's action, according to Pro Football Focus . Love has been the game's best rookie running back. The Cardinals could have gotten more from this pick had they concentrated on a different position.

4. Tennessee Titans: WR Omar Cooper Jr., Indiana

The Tennessee Titans wanted a wide receiver with this year's fourth overall pick, but they may have taken the wrong one.

To be fair, Carnell Tate has shown rapid improvement. The Ohio State product is already the Titans' leading receiver, which is what he should be. However, Tate hasn't displayed the same explosiveness or playmaking ability as Omar Cooper Jr. when the latter has been healthy.

After enduring a short stint on injured reserve due to an ankle injury, Cooper returned to the Jets lineup in Week 6 and immediately posted back-to-back 100-yard receiving games. Unlike Tate's situation, the Jets have other quality targets, specifically Garrett Wilson. Even so, Cooper is the one showing up and dazzling with his performance.

5. New York Giants: LB Arvell Reese, Ohio State

No one knew exactly where Arvell Reese would play once he joined an NFL defense. He was a hybrid at Ohio State capable of playing off-ball linebacker or working on the edge.

The New York Giants saw potential in his positional flexibility and gladly selected the standout athlete with this year's fifth overall pick. The organization remains quite happy, because Reese has been outstanding.

His usage may not be as varied as expected since he primarily serves in a true linebacker role. Though he still has more than 25 snaps kicking over the slot in coverage and over 80 working along the line of scrimmage.

As a result, Reese leads the team with 56 total tackles and 5.5 tackles for loss. Throw in 1.5 sacks, four passes defended and an interception into the mix for good measure.

The Giants linebacker serves as the prime example of this class' top picks not being found at a premium position yet making a significant impact from Day 1.

6. Kansas City Chiefs: CB Mansoor Delane, LSU

Once the Kansas City Chiefs traded Trent McDuffie to the Los Angeles Rams, the organization knew it had to replace him with a top-end man-cover corner. It did so when it traded up in this year's first round to select LSU's Mansoor Delane.

True to form, Delane has been sticky in coverage and an immediate positive within Steve Spagnuolo's defensive scheme. The Chiefs coaching staff hasn't been shy about placing the rookie on an opponent's top wide receiver. Obviously, mixed results occur. Still, the decision to do so shows a level of confidence in the first-year defensive back that's rare.

Delane entered the class as its CB1. Nothing has changed at the onset of his professional career, which made this pick the correct choice by the Chiefs.

7. Washington Commanders: S Emmanuel McNeil-Warren, Toledo

The Bleacher Report Scouting Department graded Toledo safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren as a top-20 prospect on the site's final draft board .

The MAC product fell into the second round, where he was chosen by the Cleveland Browns with this year's 58th overall pick. The Browns organization appears to have committed highway robbery now that he is on the field and making plays all over the place.

Unlike the majority of those included in this redraft, McNeil-Warren has yet to reach full-time starter status. The Browns already fielded two quality safeties before adding the 6'3", 201-pound defensive back. However, Cleveland's coaching staff finds ways to deploy McNeil-Warren.

The rookie safety can be used in a variety of roles, which makes him the ultimate chess piece. For the Washington Commanders, McNeil-Warren could have been the ideal addition to significantly improve a back end that ranks among the bottom five in pass defense for the second straight season, while also helping as an enforcer against the run.

8. New Orleans Saints: WR Carnell Tate, Ohio State

The New Orleans Saints stick with the wide receiver position, albeit a prospect without a significant injury history at the collegiate level.

Jordyn Tyson was a home run swing to potentially capture greatness because of his immense upside. However, he's yet to play this season because...you guessed it...another injury.

Granted, Tyson has dealt with a hamstring issue and will return this season. However, this scenario gives the Saints a different option with Carnell Tate still on the board.

Tate would have been an ideal complementary target opposite Chris Olave instead of being relied upon as a squad's WR1, which is the case in Tennessee with the Titans. More importantly, Tate has been on the field for every game. If available, he was the better choice despite Tyson's massive potential.

9. Cleveland Browns: OT Spencer Fano, Utah

The Cleveland Browns had no other choice but to draft their left tackle of the future with this year's ninth overall pick, because the team didn't have anyone on the roster who could play the position.

Cleveland selected Spencer Fano with the ninth overall pick, then converted him from right to left tackle. The squad's long-term blindside protector is now in place.

Fano has experienced his share of ups and downs to start his professional career, which is to be expected. As time progresses, the reigning Outland Trophy winner must become more consistent with his technique and improve his play-strength. Even so, Fano doesn't look overwhelmed or incapable of being the answer. His athleticism and movement skills have been particularly impressive.

The Browns made Fano the first offensive lineman off the board during April's draft and nothing should change from that perspective.

10. New York Giants: IOL Vega Ioane, Penn State

The New York Giants addressed their offensive line by selecting Francis Mauigoa at this spot. The concept remains mains the same, but a divergent path is taken. The reason for doing so is simple: Vega Ioane has been the game's best interior blocker among the rookie class. Mauigoa presents significant upside. He's already showed improvement, particularly as of late. However, Ioane has been a standout from Week 1, even when the Baltimore Ravens needed the guard to slide over to center, which was a position he hadn't previously played. Plus, Ioane brings the same tone-setting mentality and strength at the point of attack that the Giants wanted from Mauigoa. The previous statement isn't an indictment of the latter. Ioane is simply doing so more consistently and at a higher level.

11. Dallas Cowboys: LB Sonny Styles, Ohio State

The Dallas Cowboys had to address their defense going into the 2026 NFL draft. Despite doing so with a pair of first-round picks, the unit continues to struggle—which is why the Cowboys go in a different direction (sort of). Originally, Dallas traded up to this slot so it could select safety Caleb Downs, who graded as the No. 1 overall prospect on the Bleacher Report Scouting Department's final draft board. Downs will be discussed more in a bit. Right now, another former Buckeye, Sonny Styles, becomes the selection. Styles has points where his athleticism, length and tenacious downhill play-style make him look like a future All-Pro. His exceptional movement skills allow him to make plays all over the field. Conversely, there are times when the first-year linebacker's awareness could be better, which is why he slides outside of the Top 10. Though Dallas needs someone capable of making a difference in both phases. Styles already flashed the capability.

12. Miami Dolphins: WR Denzel Boston, Washington

Realistically, the Miami Dolphins could have gone in any direction since the organization underwent a regime change this past offseason and the team's roster was so poorly built. However, the franchise's investment in Malik Willis as its new QB1 should have precipitated a much stronger emphasis on adding to its skill positions. An investment in the offensive line by originally selecting Kadyn Proctor can't be fully argued simply because the foundation needed to be set. With only one offensive lineman off the board at this point, Miami pivots to find Willis a legitimate threat at wide receiver. Denzel Boston automatically brings the frame and capabilities of a true X-receiver. He currently leads the Cleveland Browns with 372 receiving yards and three touchdown receptions. Both figures would lead the Dolphins, too. Meanwhile, Willis would have a big-framed target to consistently target instead of the mishmash Miami currently features at wide receiver.

13. Los Angeles Rams: LB Jacob Rodriguez, Texas Tech

Maybe Ty Simpson will be a franchise quarterback one day. The Los Angeles Rams are all-in for this season, though.

The roster needed help beyond a successor to Matthew Stafford. An instant-impact defender could have gone a long way to helping the Rams right now.

The organization subsequently added Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald to its defensive front, which obviously changed the math. Even so, an opportunity to add someone like Texas Tech's Jacob Rodriguez should have been under more serious consideration.

Rodriguez would have fit nicely alongside Nate Landman. The rookie currently leads the Miami Dolphins, who selected the linebacker with this year's 43rd overall pick, with 61 total tackles.

Rodriguez has a nose for the football and a penchant for creating turnovers, which could have been the ultimate complementary piece to Los Angeles' offense.

14. Baltimore Ravens: IOL Keylan Rutledge, Georgia Tech

Tyler Linderbaum's departure in free agency dictated the Baltimore Ravens' draft course. While Vega Ioane didn't directly replace the Pro Bowl center (at first), the Ravens approached the addition of a high-end guard prospect as fortifying their offensive interior. The logic is sound. In this scenario, Ioane is already off the board. Keylan Rutledge could provide the same guard-center flexibility along the interior as the team's actual first-round selection. Eventually, Ioane did have to take over at center due to injuries. Rutledge may have started every game at left guard this season, but he spent extensive time at center during training camp and the preseason. Furthermore, Rutledge brings a rare combination of toughness and power at the point of attack, thus also giving the Ravens exactly what they needed.

15. Tampa Bay Buccaneers: Edge R Mason Thomas, Oklahoma

Some will argue that the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' actual first-round selection, Rueben Bain Jr., is the biggest disappointment from this year's draft class. Though injuries certainly played their part. But no one can deny that Bain has been slow to adjust to the pro game. Thus, the Bucs look at a different edge-rusher with a better track record to start his career.

R Mason Thomas is a relentless pass-rusher. His first-step quickness, closing speed and tenacity already make him a handful for NFL offensive tackles, even as a rookie. Thomas' 19 pressures rank third among his classmates, according to Pro Football Focus . Thomas lining up opposite YaYa Diaby brings far more juice to Todd Bowles' aggressive defensive approach.

16. New York Jets: WR KC Concepcion, Texas A&M

Take a bow, Andrew Berry, because KC Concepcion is now the fourth Cleveland Browns rookie found among the top-16 of this NFL redraft. Concepcion currently leads the Browns with 30 receptions. Cleveland's coaching staff manufactures touches for the first-year pass-catcher because of his open-field explosiveness and ability to create in space. Those same traits make him an ideal fit alongside Garrett Wilson.

The New York Jets are already getting the same thing from Omar Cooper Jr., at least in recent weeks. But he's not available in this scenario. Concepcion can fill the same role and give the Jets another talented target for whenever the franchise finally finds its long-term answer at quarterback. The Browns general manager basically took the same approach as the Jets, though Cleveland has proven to be more successful in the short term.

17. Detroit Lions: CB Avieon Terrell, Clemson

The Detroit Lions' pass defense is atrocious and easily the league's worst, yet the organization chose not to address its secondary until the fifth round. Let's rectify that situation.

Offensive tackle remains a sticking point without Blake Miller's selection at this slot. The Lions actually passed on Avieon Terrell twice during the draft. The fact the organization did so was surprising, because Terrell was arguably the most competitive individual among his respective position group.

Considering the state of the Lions' secondary and Terrell's play-style, he'd be a natural fit in Detroit. Plus, the Clemson product adds flexibility to the unit since he can play out wide or over the slot. Terrell has allowed the second-lowest passer rating into his coverage among rookies, according to Pro Football Network . Ironically, the Lions' Keith Abney II is first. Though Terrell has played nearly 100 more snaps so far.

18. Minnesota Vikings: DL Gracen Halton, Oklahoma

The Minnesota Vikings wanted an athletic, explosive interior difference-maker for their defensive line, hence the selection of Caleb Banks. But Banks had significant concerns regarding foot issues. So far, Banks has played more than 20 snaps in only one game as the Vikings ease him into the defensive line rotation.

Meanwhile, Gracen Halton already emerged as a starter along the San Francisco 49ers defensive line. Going into this past weekend's contest, Halton graded among the league's top run-stuffers, according to Pro Football Network . The previous statistic wasn't just for rookies, either. Halton is in the same conversation as Jeffery Simmons, Dexter Lawrence, Quinnen Williams and DeForest Buckner. The fourth-round rookie's snap count may decrease with Buckner's addition to the Niners' lineup, but Halton already proved he's disruptive enough to consistently reset the line of scrimmage.

19. Carolina Panthers: OT Max Iheanachor, Arizona State

The Carolina Panthers' offensive tackle situation was in disarray.

Left tackle Ikem Ekwonu continues to recover from a ruptured patellar tendon. Meanwhile, veteran right tackle Taylor Moton had been diagnosed with blood clots prior to the start of the 2026 campaign.

Carolina did sink this pick into an offensive tackle, Monroe Freeling, but Max Iheanachor was the better bet among the developmental options.

Freeling has an elite athletic profile. He survived when asked to start in Week 1. Conversely, Iheanachor didn't open the season in the Pittsburgh Steelers lineup but eventually became the squad's starting right tackle.

Iheanachor's presence has made a difference. The Steelers are now more athletic and nasty at the point of attack, which gives him the edge for this particular slotting.

20. Philadelphia Eagles: WR Germie Bernard, Alabama

This specific pairing drips with irony based on how the 2026 NFL draft actually unfolded, but the result is similar. The Philadelphia Eagles traded ahead of the Pittsburgh Steelers when general manager Howie Roseman caught wind of the latter's preference to select wide receiver Makai Lemon. A deal was struck to leap over the Steelers so the Eagles could choose Lemon. Lemon has been solid in Philadelphia. His toughness working over the middle of the field has been particularly impressive. But Germie Bernard, whom the Steelers chose in the second round after missing out on Lemon's selection, is more explosive and a sharper route-runner. The fact Bernard has quickly earned the trust of quarterback Aaron Rodgers says a lot about how advanced he is. Thus, he gets the edge to help the Eagles offset AJ Brown's loss.

21. Pittsburgh Steelers: WR Makai Lemon, USC

In this scenario, the Pittsburgh Steelers land exactly who they originally targeted this past April.

Makai Lemon was the Steelers' original plan to pair with DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. Things worked out OK after the team landed offensive tackle Max Iheanachor and wide receiver Germie Bernard in the first two rounds. This situation is different, though.

As a result, the Steelers are fortunate to land their preferred target.

Lemon's fearlessness working the middle of the field would significantly benefit quarterback Aaron Rodgers, especially after Pittman ended up on injured reserve due to a foot injury. The rookie could become the security blanket Rodgers needs since the 42-year-old has struggled to push the ball down the field this season.

22. Los Angeles Chargers: IOL Austin Barber, Florida

The Los Angeles Chargers drafted a former Florida Gator to address their offensive interior. The organization should have looked elsewhere along the same collegiate unit. Los Angeles chose Jake Slaughter during the second round to be the starting point of the position's fortifications. The organization drafted four blockers, yet the unit is still not fixed. Once again, injuries have played a significant part, but the position group's depth should have been drastically improved. Initially, Slaughter was earmarked to play guard, but a season-ending injury to Tyler Biadasz caused the rookie to move back over the ball. Austin Barber doesn't have that same versatility, though he successfully converted from offensive tackle to guard with the Cleveland Browns. Barber has started every game at right guard so far. Conversely, the Chargers have already started three different left guards. Or the rookie could be an outright upgrade over right guard Cole Strange. Either way, Los Angeles' front five would be better than it is now.

23. Dallas Cowboys: S Caleb Downs, Ohio State

The Dallas Cowboys passed on Caleb Downs earlier in favor of linebacker Sonny Styles, who was still available in this scenario. The team doubles back and still lands Downs. Once again, the Ohio State safety entered the draft class as its No. 1 overall prospect regardless of position. His value was predicated on his football IQ and ability to serve as an eraser along the back line. Due to the Cowboys' scatterbrained approach defensively, Downs hasn't created as much of an impact as expected. Though he's still been quite good when looking at his performance in a vacuum. Downs leads the Cowboys with 48 total tackles and three forced fumbles. He can be the field general for the entire unit, but his standing within the group remains a work in progress as he feels his way through coverage responsibilities.

24. Cleveland Browns: WR Antonio Williams, Clemson

The Cleveland Browns have drafted extremely well over the last two years, which is a significant reason why the team currently owns a 5-2 record and sits atop the AFC North.

Case in point, five different Browns have already been mentioned in this redraft. So, the team is forced to look elsewhere and lands on a different wide receiver since KC Concepcion is no longer available.

Cleveland had two glaring needs entering the 2026 draft class. Offensive tackle was already addressed. The roster also required significant help at wide receiver, hence the Concepcion selection.

Clemson's Antonio Williams brings a similar skill set as a receiver using his explosiveness and athleticism to create after the catch. With Terry McLaurin now out for the season, Williams should experience a significant usage increase with the Washington Commanders, but the flashes of what he can do to opposing defenses have already been apparent.

25. Chicago Bears: Edge Cashius Howell, Texas A&M

The Chicago Bears knew they didn't have enough along their defensive front, hence why the team jumped at the opportunity to add Jeffery Simmons prior to this year's trade deadline. Granted, Simmons is one of the league's best defenders. At the same time, the Bears had a glaring need up front, specifically at defensive end, and failed to properly address it.

Even after Simmons' addition, the Bears could have still done more at defensive end.

Entering this past weekend's game, Cashius Howell ranked second among rookies in pass-rush win rate . The reigning SEC Defensive Player of the Year is smooth and fluid turning the edge, with a motor that doesn't stop. He has a pass-rush plan and attacks. Howell may not have started—he hasn't with the Cincinnati Bengals—but he would have added significant juice as part of sub-packages.

26. Houston Texans: RB Jeremiyah Love, Notre Dame

The Houston Texans have found themselves in the upside-down. Preseason expectations have been completely flipped.

The Texans defense was supposed to dominate, while the offense was questionable. Well, the opposite has happened this fall. Still, Houston's offense features less talent overall, hence the selection of Jeremiyah Love.

Yes, the Texans traded for David Montgomery this offseason. Love is a different type of running back, whose value adds to both phases of the game. As a result, he was graded as the No. 2 overall prospect entering the draft by the Bleacher Report Scouting Department.

Love leads all rookies with 67 carries and 245 yards. The Arizona Cardinals have used him sparingly as a pass-catcher despite investing this year's third overall pick in the reigning Doak Walker Award winner.

Most teams earlier in the process had other areas that could be addressed, with options that have flourished. The Texans find themselves in a fortunate situation where they can select a running back capable of being the team's offensive focal point.

27. Miami Dolphins: IOL Kadyn Proctor, Alabama

The Miami Dolphins originally drafted Kadyn Proctor with this year's 12th overall pick. He's been solid, with flashes of what he could become as a physical tone-setter for Miami's offense. The 6'7", 352-pound rookie also experienced his fair share of mistakes to start his career, which is expected. The up-and-down nature of Proctor's rookie performance made the decision to look at a different position during Miami's initial first-round selection more realistic. Earlier, the Dolphins added wide receiver Denzel Boston to provide quarterback Malik Willis with a legitimate No. 1 threat in the passing game. Proctor's availability later in the process is a fortunate outcome to ensure the trenches still get built properly. The collegiate offensive tackle transitioned to guard relatively well, while retaining significant growth potential.

28. New England Patriots: Edge Malachi Lawrence, UCF

Caleb Lomu will be Will Campbell's long-term bookend as the New England Patriots' right tackle. However, the idea of the Patriots investing in a third offensive tackle (also behind veteran Morgan Moses) coming off a losing Super Bowl trip, while trading up to do so, is the height of hubris. Yes, Lomu is talented. Yes, Moses is in his mid-30s. Yes, the rookie has started a game already due to injuries. But this team had glaring deficiencies despite their run to Super Bowl LX and a developmental offensive tackle could have been taken later. Specifically, the Patriots' medical staff would have informed team decision-makers about Harold Landry's ongoing knee issues. A quick glance at the depth chart would then have shown the team needed to beef up its pass rush. Fortunately, Gabe Jacas was available in the second round. He's not in this scenario. Malachi Lawrence has the length, athleticism and flexibility to eventually be a premier edge-rusher. He's definitely flashed getting after opposing quarterbacks, which is exactly what the Patriots need.

29. Kansas City Chiefs: OT Caleb Lomu, Utah

Unlike the New England Patriots, who actually chose Caleb Lomu a pick earlier, the Kansas City Chiefs desperately needed to address offensive tackle. In an ironic twist, Kansas City may have found a solution to one of its offensive tackle spots in undrafted free agent Kahlil Benson, who required a rookie minicamp tryout to get signed. Benson isn't included in this redraft despite holding down Kansas City's left tackle spot, because he often requires significant help from the offensive scheme to protect him as a pass-blocker. By contrast, Lomu's natural movement skills made him into a first-round draft pick despite subpar play-strength. Thus, the Chiefs would be set at one and possibly both offensive tackle spots depending on Josh Simmons' maturation.

30. New York Jets: TE Eli Raridon, Notre Dame

Raridon is a more natural in-line option to play alongside Mason Taylor, who has taken more snaps from the slot than first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq this season. Sadiq's upside is immense. He's an athlete unlike any other at the tight end position. But athleticism only goes so far depending on how it's utilized. In this particular case, the New York Jets could have added a prospect that made more sense within the scope of their personnel and offensive scheme. At this point, the third-round tight end has slightly more receiving yards despite fewer reps in the pass game compared to the class' actual TE1. Raridon does benefit from playing alongside quarterback Drake Maye. But he also capitalizes more often when opportunities arise, while presenting the type of skill set that would mesh nicely in New York.

31. Tennessee Titans: OT Markel Bell, Miami

The Tennessee Titans chose to trade back into the first round for a developmental defensive lineman, Keldric Faulk, who hasn't performed particularly well in a rotational role. Instead, the Titans could have fortified a porous offensive front to help in quarterback Cam Ward's development. At best, left tackle Dan Moore Jr. is a replacement-level performer.

In Markel Bell, the Tennessee Titans could have gotten another massive blocker to bookend right tackle JC Latham and likely given Ward a wider pocket from which to work.

Bell has been forced to replace Lane Johnson after the future Hall of Fame inductee's abrupt retirement. But the 6'9", 346-pound rookie's performance over the last four games has been promising.

It's not surprising either, because Bell showed tremendous growth over the entirety of the 2025 campaign as the Miami Hurricanes' left tackle. He's continued that ascending path.

32. Seattle Seahawks: RB Kaelon Black, Indiana

The Seattle Seahawks didn't have a choice but to draft a running back after Kenneth Walker III left in free agency and Zach Charbonnet suffered a torn ACL in January.

The franchise settled on Notre Dame's Jadarian Price. Unfortunately, Price injured his chest, which forced an early-season trip to the injured reserve. With Jeremiyah Love already off the board, third-round ball-carrier Kaelon Black has been the league's second-best rookie runner. Black served as the Indiana Hoosiers' closer during their national championship season. The 5'9", 211-pound back makes decisive cuts and always falls forward through contact. Despite Christian McCaffrey on the same roster, the San Francisco 49ers coaching staff has made sure to get Black involved and take some pressure off their 30-year-old lead back. The RB2's 233 rushing yards are only 12 behind Love's output.

articles.title: Before Olivia Ponton, there was Olivia Holzmacher: inside Joe Burrow’s seven-year love story that began at Ohio State
articles.summary: Joe Burrow's love life has become a regular topic since reports linked him to model Olivia Ponton in December 2024.
articles.body: Joe Burrow's love life has become a regular topic since reports linked him to model Olivia Ponton in December 2024. Before that, though, the Bengals quarterback spent about seven years with Olivia Holzmacher, a relationship that started at Ohio State in 2017. They stayed together through his move to LSU, a Heisman Trophy and an NFL career, then split quietly in 2024. Neither has explained why. Neither has said much at all, which is part of how this story took off. Fans filled the silence themselves. Here's what is actually on the record.Joe Burrow's seven-year relationship with Olivia Holzmacher began at Ohio StateBurrow enrolled at Ohio State in 2015 and did not join the football team until 2016. Even then he spent two years as a backup. Holzmacher came into the picture in August 2017, right in the middle of that wait. The relationship was already running before anyone outside Columbus cared much about him.Then he left. Burrow graduated in 2018 with a degree in consumer and family financial services and transferred to LSU, which meant Baton Rouge instead of Columbus. They kept dating from a distance. Holzmacher made the trip often to watch him play.Those trips lined up with the best stretch of his football life. He won the Heisman Trophy in 2019, then the national title in January 2020. Not many long-distance couples get a run like that to share.The pattern held after the Cincinnati Bengals drafted him. Holzmacher was often seen cheering from his private suite at Paycor Stadium. Engagement talk came up in 2023 and again in 2024, and it never went anywhere official. No announcement came from either of them.The split was just as quiet. It is still unclear exactly when it happened, and neither side has addressed it. Sports Illustrated noted that fans began wondering after the two had not been seen together in public since January 2024. The silence did the rest.How the Olivia Ponton reports beganThe Ponton story started with a break-in. On Monday, December 9, 2024, Burrow's home was broken into while he was in Dallas for a game. A police report said Ponton arrived at the house, found a broken window and a ransacked bedroom, and called 911. The same report listed her as Burrow's employee. That wording raised eyebrows, though it proved nothing about what they were to each other.A source told People the two had been hooking up since the fall and were keeping it casual. That is about as close as the public has gotten to an explanation, and it came from an unnamed person, not from Burrow or Ponton.They showed up in the same places in 2025. Paparazzi video from the Miami Grand Prix on May 4 showed them leaving events in the same van more than once. The next day Burrow made his Met Gala debut. Ponton did not walk the carpet with him, but both were seen at after-parties that night. Reporters asked her about Burrow. She kept her head down.Ponton, now 24, is a model who made her Sports Illustrated debut in 2022 and has worked with brands like Calvin Klein and Skims. She has a large online following, yet she has stayed quiet about Burrow.The public record is lopsided. One side is seven years of football seasons, road trips and suite seats. The other is a police report, a source's comment and a few paparazzi clips, and no word from Burrow or Ponton.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
