articles.title: WWE's Paul Heyman Reacts to Christian Watson's Return from Hospital for Packers in Trending Post
articles.summary: Christian Watson's return to Lambeau Field in an ambulance during the Green Bay Packers' 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers on Thursday Night Football caught the attention of WWE Hall of Famer Paul Heyman.
articles.body:
Christian Watson's return to Lambeau Field in an ambulance during the Green Bay Packers' 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers on Thursday Night Football caught the attention of WWE Hall of Famer Paul Heyman.

Heyman, as only he can, drew a comparison to WCW Clash of the Champions XVII when Sting left the arena early in the night after being attacked by Lex Luger only to return later by stealing the ambulance that took him away for his scheduled match with Rick Rude.

Watson was taken off the field in the second quarter and transported to a hospital via ambulance when he landed hard catching a 53-yard pass. He was diagnosed with a broken rib and was coughing up blood, but told reporters after the game it felt like he was watching something out of a WWE.

The ambulance's departure and return to Lambeau took less than an hour. ESPN's Rob Demovsky noted Watson was in the ambulance around 8:30 p.m. local time, then back on the sideline by 9:19 p.m.

Even with the injury scare, Watson finished the game with 113 yards on a season-high eight receptions. He put up that stat line despite playing a season-low 34 offensive snaps.

One key difference between Watson's situation and the Sting-Rude match referenced by Heyman is the outcome. Green Bay won to earn their fourth victory in the last five games.

Sting, on the other hand, was unable to triumph in his heroic return. Rude, who was managed by Heyman at the time, defeated the Icon to win the United States championship.

articles.title: Josh Allen vs Lamar Jackson: Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens resume rivalry as NFL greats knock at Super Bowl door again - NFL Gameday Guide
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens are hoping to welcome Lamar Jackson back from injury as they take on Josh Allen's Buffalo Bills in a clash of Super Bowl contenders, live on Sky Sports+ from 5.30pm this Sunday, followed by Kansas City Chiefs against Denver Broncos
articles.body:
That is providing Jackson does in fact make his return from an injury that has sidelined him for the past three weeks; either way, it remains a story of parallels and a mutual Arrowhead enemy.

One might rightly point to the demise of Andy Reid's side in recent years, but were it not for the Chiefs' monopoly on the AFC for much of the last decade then one of Allen or Jackson - maybe even both - would be proud owners of a ring with which to complement their MVP accolades.

Since 2020, Buffalo have lost twice in the AFC Championship Game and four times in the Divisional Round of the playoffs, four of those defeats coming against the Chiefs. In the same period, Baltimore have twice lost to the Bills in the Divisional Round as well as falling to the Chiefs at the 2023 AFC Championship Game.

The Bills (5-1) host the Ravens (4-3) this weekend, live on Sky Sports, in the latest collision of two perennial contenders all-too familiar with final hurdle stumbles.

The Bills have toppled the Ravens on three straight occasions at home, the latest being last season's Week One thriller as Buffalo scored 16 unanswered points in the final four minutes to overturn a 15-point deficit in their 41-40 victory. It was a game befitting of a Super Bowl stage itself.

Before then the two met at the AFC Divisional Round in January 2025, when the Bills escaped with a 27-25 win following the infamous end zone drop by Mark Andrews for what would have been a game-tying two-point conversion.

Powerhouse offenses are piloted by Hall of Fame-destined quarterbacks, and yet their wait for a shot at the big dance goes on.

There is an argument for there being no two players in the league greater at hiding their team's weaknesses or dictating their team's success than Allen or Jackson; they are unrivalled equalisers, game-tilting deciders.

Allen has been electric through seven weeks of the season, throwing for 1,504 yards and nine touchdowns to four interceptions with a passer rating of 102.1 while ranking second in EPA/play and fifth in success rate. He also leads all quarterbacks with 240 rushing yards, eight rushing touchdowns and 23 first down runs. Nobody is better at strapping an entire organisation to their back.

This Bills offense has a case for being the best he has played in, ranking third in total yards, 12th in passing, second in rushing, first in scoring, first in EPA/play, third in success rate, first in dropback EPA and third in rush EPA under Joe Brady, who replaced Sean McDermott as head coach in January.

It isn't all Allen, either. James Cook remains the perfect backfield partner to his quarterback as Brady's trusted jab with which to tee up his play-action haymaker, amassing a third-most 627 yards and six touchdowns at 104.5 yards per game from 117 carries.

But we have been here before. A big bully offense stomping on the league while harbouring a defense with a proclivity for playoff disappointment. Allen could be near flawless all year, and yet knows come the postseason that one turnover might prove costly, such is the lack of trust in things on the other side of the ball.

Buffalo sought to address as much this offseason by hiring Jim Leonard as their new defensive coordinator - the immediate results have been ugly. The Bills currently sit second-worst in total yards allowed, passing, EPA/play and pressure rate, while ranking 15th against the run and second from last in scoring.

For the Ravens the availability of their star player remains a leading hindrance having been without Jackson for the last three games due to an ankle injury.

Caution with his return is crucial as they consider the bigger picture of a playoff push further down the line, particularly with a quarterback who not only feasts from the pocket but functions heavily on his ground threat and off-platform creativity.

Sure, it is an injury some might play with. But not everybody plays like Lamar Jackson, who has every right to remain on the sideline until comfortable he can protect himself.

There seems to be a bizarre conspiracy theory among certain corners of the media regarding Jackson's injury layoffs, and an over-eagerness to see him rushed back even were it to his detriment. Still, Jackson has missed 17 games through injury since his first year as full-time starter in 2019, the impact of which is evidenced through the Ravens failing to reach the playoffs in two of the three seasons in which he has missed four or more games, per ESPN stats.

"He's been one of the best if not the best quarterback. And what he's consistently done when he's on the field is unbelievable," said Allen of Jackson. "He's a very special player and I've got so much respect for him. "That's why you play this game is to have matchups like this."

He is set to return to the lineup to replace Tyler Huntley this weekend having produced a flying start to the season by completing 68 of 96 passes (70.8 per cent) for 967 yards and six touchdowns to just one interception. He even still ranks first in EPA/play and second in success rate. It was MVP-brewing Lamar, only to be slowed by injury. When he suffers, the Ravens suffer.

"Oh, man, you know Lamar, Lamar wants to play. He wants to play when he is fully healthy," said wide receiver Zay Flowers. "And seeing him out there today (Thursday), obviously it gave everybody a smile on their face."

Baltimore arrive on the back of a 35-13 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, during which Jesse Minter's side blew a 13-point half-time lead. It would see them become the first team ever to lose by 20 points after leading by 13 at the break, while also marking the 17th game they have lost after holding a double-digit lead since 2020. They have a Jekyll and Hyde problem on defense, their secondary in particular warranting criticism and lacking the talent required to combat the elite quarterbacks that would await in the playoffs.

Jackson's absence has also contributed to a disappointing run for Derrick Henry, who has managed just 103 rushing yards over the past two games and is averaging a career-low 3.9 yards per carry. Bizarrely, he is also among the worst in the league on short yardage situations

Two teams with sledgehammers at quarterback. But two teams with lingering questions when it comes to Super Bowl credentials.

The Ravens gave Zay Flowers a four-year, $140m contract extension in the offseason, and in return he is delivering a breakout season as a field-flipping focal point to Declan Doyle's offense. Flowers has been a menace with the ball in hand, his 321 yards after the catch bettered only by Jaylen Warren's 350.

The 2023 first-round pick has caught 40 of his 53 targets for a fourth-most 608 yards and three touchdowns while averaging a second-most 101.3 yards per game, second only to reigning Offensive Player of the Year Jaxon Smith-Njigba. He managed eight catches for 137 yards and a touchdown in last weekend's defeat to the Bengals, his rise to a place among the NFL's elite wide receivers crucial to Balitmore's playoff charge.

Reigniting the running game to control the clock and the line of scrimmage through Henry, and the return of Lamar Jackson, is what the Ravens need in order to continue feeding Flowers out of play-action.

Kenneth Walker ran into the NFL's best defense last week as his former team and Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks bottled him up for just 36 rushing yards in Kansas City's 20-3 loss. This weekend the Chiefs running back, one of the league's very best through contact, faces a Denver Broncos defense that leads the NFL in missed tackles; in fact, the Broncos missed 28 tackles for 247 yards when the sides met earlier this season, Walker gaining 173 yards on that occasion and 144 after contact, according to NextGen Stats.

Denver are seeking their own source of joy on the ground as they enter the game ranked ninth-worst in rushing yards per game, Jonah Coleman trending towards an enhanced role should J.K. Dobbins continue to struggle. A backfield spike is needed as Sean Payton looks to restore the best of Bo Nix, who is playing with a career-low completion percentage and finding it tough to push the ball downfield.

The Los Angeles Rams and Chargers may call the same city and the same stadium home, but the two are a chasm apart when it comes to realistic ambitions this season. Sean McVay's Rams are still trying to get their season up and running after a 3-4 start amid soaring expectations as Super Bowl favourites. They arrive off a 35-21 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, with MVP Matthew Stafford leading the NFL with 1,989 passing yards and Puka Nacua riding a streak of 15 straight games with at least five receptions as their centrepiece on offense.

McVay knows any further slips up must be avoided in a hotly-contested NFC West division, and so the Chargers pose as something of a punching bag as the only winless team in the league at 0-6. Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh has not lost seven games in a row since he played quarterback for the 2000 San Diego Chargers. Only Aaron Rodgers and Deshaun Watson have been sacked more times than the 21 taken by Justin Herbert, who has endured a miserable start while completing just 107 of 180 passes (59.4 per cent) for 1,141 yards and five touchdowns to eight interceptions for a league-worst passer rating of 68.8 among qualified starters. Mike McDaniel remains the play-caller, for now. Their season is over. But how bad will it get?

The rivalry is real between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns, who are tied for the lead on 5-2 at the top of the AFC North ahead of both the Bengals and Ravens.

Browns edge rusher Jared Verse caused a stir earlier this season when he criticised for the Steelers for playing dirty after Cleveland's 27-24 win.

"I don't got no respect for anybody that plays too dirty, and that does too much extra s*** after the game," he said.

"I can't wait until we see them again," Verse added. "I'm going to put that one on the calendar. I can't wait to get my hands on them again."

Steelers stalwart defensive lineman Cam Heyward hit back this week, welcoming a shot at revenge as Pittsburgh arrive back from their victory over the New Orleans Saints in Paris.

"Double teaming, sliding, chipping, are those not allowed in our game?" Heyward said on The Rich Eisen Show. " Yeah, I got the bruises to prove it. But we don't whine about it, baby. It's part of the game. And so, I'm looking forward to this game. It's gonna be a fun game. Both teams are in position to do a lot of work in this division, as they say. The AFC North is on fire and I'm glad I'm in the kitchen because I like it that way. But those are words that were said and they will be addressed."

The Colts traded All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson to the Super Bowl champion Seahawks, and veteran defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the 49ers.

The Titans traded All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears for 2027 and 2028 first-round picks as well as a 2027 fourth-round pick.

The Chiefs signed former Ravens kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad; Tucker served a 10-game suspension last season for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy following allegations of sexual misconduct.

Jay-Z announced that he will headline the Super Bowl LXI half-time show at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California in February.

Bears pass rusher Montez Sweat is clear to return from a two-game suspension for violating the league's performance-enhancing substance policy.

Lions QB Jared Goff needs 212 passing yards and no interceptions to become the fourth player since 1980 with at least 2,000 passing yards and no interceptions to begin a season.

Ravens RB Derrick Henry needs a touchdown to tie Marshall Faulk (136) for the fourth-most touchdowns by a running back in NFL history.

With at least 100 receiving yards against the Chargers, Rams receiver Puka Nacua can surpass A.J. Green (20 games) for the third-most games with at least 100 receiving yards by a player in his first four seasons in NFL history.

Chiefs TE Travis Kelce leads the NFL with 1,104 receptions in 193 career games since entering the NFL in 2013.

Bengals QB Joe Burrow needs three touchdown passes in a game to overtake Peyton Manning (32) for the third-most games of such kind by a player in his first seven seasons, behind Dan Marino (42) and Patrick Mahomes (38).

articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs may have to rethink their plans to strengthen Patrick Mahomes’ receiving corps as the NFL trade deadline approaches.
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs may have to rethink their plans to strengthen Patrick Mahomes’ receiving corps as the NFL trade deadline approaches. Tyreek Hill’s much-discussed return to Kansas City is beginning to look less certain, with concerns over his recovery and off-field situation reportedly influencing the team's thinking. While a reunion would bring back a familiar face, the Chiefs appear increasingly open to exploring other options. One name gaining attention is Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs, who could offer Kansas City another route out of its growing offensive problems.Tyreek Hill’s injury concerns complicate potential Chiefs reunionHill's possible return to Kansas City has attracted considerable attention, particularly with the Chiefs struggling to find consistency among their wide receivers. However, his recovery from a serious knee injury has created doubts about how much he could contribute during the remainder of the 2026 season.NFL insider Ian Rapoport recently suggested that the Chiefs are unlikely to make an aggressive move for Hill while his situation remains uncertain. Speaking on ESPN's Big Day, he explained that Kansas City could still pursue a receiver but might not take a chance on an injured player.“We’ll see what kind. It’s. not like Justin Jefferson is out there. Tyreek Hill is not healthy enough, and there is obviously all the off the field stuff,” Ian Rapoport commented on ESPN’s Big Day. “I would expect them to target a receiver, we’ll see at what level. But [general manager] Brett Veach is always trying to invest and help, I think that’s where they go.”These concerns could push general manager Brett Veach towards a safer option before the deadline. Hill remains a popular figure among Chiefs supporters, but sentiment alone may not be enough to convince the organisation to bring him back.Josh Downs emerges as potential Chiefs trade targetIndianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs has entered the conversation as a possible alternative. According to Daniel Arwas of Heavy, former NFL player and analyst Jeff Saturday identified Downs as a name worth watching if Kansas City decides to pursue help from Indianapolis.“Jeff Saturday subsequently touted current Colts slot Josh Downs as a name to watch as a possible addition for Kansas City,” via Daniel Arwas on Heavy. “Hill’s injury and off the field issues may complicate the signing altogether, it once again feels more and more likely that Kansas City will look to alternative options rather than risking dipping their toe back in the Tyreek Hill fountain.“The potential interest makes sense when looking at Kansas City's current receiving options. Rashee Rice has missed two consecutive games with a hamstring injury, while Tyquan Thornton is dealing with a potentially season-ending issue. Xavier Worthy has also struggled to deliver consistent performances.The Chiefs are 5-1 through seven weeks, but their recent offensive struggles have exposed a weakness that could become costly as the season progresses. Kenneth Walker has helped keep the offence moving, yet Mahomes needs more dependable targets in the passing game.Kansas City cannot afford to wait much longer. articles.title: Several Eagles Players Reportedly 'Could Be Had' at NFL Trade Deadline amid Latest Rumors
articles.summary: Having already traded Cam Jurgens amid their five-game losing streak, the Philadelphia Eagles figure to be active leading up to the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
articles.body:
Having already traded Cam Jurgens amid their five-game losing streak, the Philadelphia Eagles figure to be active leading up to the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

According to Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer , a number of Eagles players with expiring contracts "could be had" with just over one week remaining before the deadline.

Breer specifically cited Marquise Brown, Riq Woolen and Dallas Goedert as contract-year players who Philadelphia might deal.

Re-Drafting 2026 NFL Draft Entering Week 8

Saquon Barkley is the biggest name on the Eagles who has been bantered about as a potential trade candidate, but Breer described that as "less likely" in part because of injuries that have limited his availability this season.

It's perhaps notable that trading Barkley would also incur a $26 million dead-cap charge for the Eagles in 2027.

Breer also noted the Eagles have told other teams that defensive tackle Moro Ojomo, another player set to hit free agency after this season, is not available as they could look to sign him in the offseason.

The way this season has gone in Philadelphia already, there's no reason for general manager Howie Roseman not to test the waters to see what offers might be out there.

Brown has been a bust due to injuries that have limited him to two games. He has just two catches for 30 yards and has played a total of 53 snaps . Woolen has been more miss than hit in coverage.

Goedert has remained productive in an otherwise disappointing passing game for the Eagles. He ranks top three on the team in receptions (22), receiving yards (228) and touchdown receptions (two).

None of the three players mentioned will likely bring back a huge return, but Roseman was able to negotiate a future second-round pick from the Baltimore Ravens for Jurgens.

History has shown underestimating Roseman is not a smart bet for anyone, especially if he is trying to make moves that set the Eagles up for a quick turnaround amid what looks like a lost 2026 season.

articles.title: Records, Milestones, and History: NFL skill players to watch in Week 8
articles.summary: Week 8 in the NFL will be the week for skill players to move up the record books
articles.body:
Week 8 in the NFL will be the week for skill players to move up the record books. We've already looked at the QBs set to do so; now, let's focus on the RBs, WRs.

Detroit running back Jahmyr Gibbs has 58 scrimmage touchdowns (46 rushing, 12 receiving) since entering the NFL in 2023.

With a touchdown on Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings , Gibbs can surpass Pro Football Hall of Famer Marcus Allen (58 touchdowns) and tie Alvin Kamara (59) for the third-most touchdowns by a player in his first four seasons in NFL history. Only Pro Football Hall of Famers Terrell Davis (61 touchdowns) and LaDainian Tomlinson (60) have more.

Baltimore running back Derrick Henry leads the NFL with 135 scrimmage touchdowns (129 rushing, six receiving) since entering the league in 2016.

With at least two touchdowns on Sunday at the Buffalo Bills , Henry – who has 37 career games with multiple touchdowns – can surpass Pro Football Hall of Famer Randy Moss (37 games) for the fourth-most games with multiple touchdowns in NFL history, trailing only Pro Football Hall of Famers Jerry Rice (46), LaDainian Tomlinson (44) and Emmitt Smith (39).

Atlanta running back Bijan Robinson, 24, leads the NFL with 907 scrimmage yards and is tied for the second-most games with at least 100 scrimmage yards (five) this season.

With at least 100 scrimmage yards at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, Robinson can become the fifth player with 35 games with at least 100 scrimmage yards under the age of 25 in NFL history, joining Clinton Portis (40 games), Ezekiel Elliott (38), as well as Pro Football Hall of Famers Edgerrin James (39) and Emmitt Smith (35)

Cincinnati wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase – set to appear in his 85th career game in Week 8 – is tied for the lead with 59 touchdown receptions since entering the NFL in 2021.

With a touchdown reception on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans , Chase can become the fourth player with 60 touchdown receptions in his first 85 career games in the Super Bowl era, joining Pro Football Hall of Famers Jerry Rice (77 touchdown receptions), Randy Moss (66), and Rob Gronkowski (67).

Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua has 20 games with at least 100 receiving yards since entering the NFL in 2023.

With at least 100 receiving yards against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, Nacua can surpass A.J. Green (20 games) for the third-most games with at least 100 receiving yards by a player in his first four seasons in NFL history. Only Justin Jefferson (29 games) and Pro Football Hall of Famer Randy Moss (23) have more.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba - Seattle Seahawks, WR

Seattle wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba leads the NFL in receiving yards (867) and touchdown receptions (eight) and ranks second in receptions (58) in 2026.

With 133 receiving yards on Monday Night Football against the Chicago Bears , Smith-Njigba can become the sixth player ever with at least 1,000 receiving yards in his first eight games of a season, joining Charlie Hennigan (1,122 with the Houston Oilers in 1961), Pro Football Hall of Famer Elroy "Crazy legs" Hirsch (1,058 with the Los Angeles Rams in 1951), Wes Chandler (1,032 with Atlanta in 1982), Pro Football Hall of Famer Don Hutson (1,032 with Green Bay in 1942) and Tyreek Hill (1,104 with Miami in 2023).

Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown leads the league with 593 receptions since he entered the NFL in 2021.

With five receptions on Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings, St. Brown, who has 67 career games with at least 5 receptions since 2021, can tie CeeDee Lamb (68) for the most games with at least 5 receptions by a player in his first six seasons.

articles.title: Bold quarterback predictions in NFL Week 8: Dak Prescott, Jared Goff & more
articles.summary: Dak. Goff and more QB predictions for Week 8 of the NFL season.
articles.body:
Touchdown passes look wonderfully democratic on the stat sheet. A perfect throw through traffic counts exactly the same as a tight end wandering unattended into the end zone. NFL quarterbacks understand this arrangement better than anyone. Week 8 offers opportunities to exploit it – and one defense prepared to make every completion feel expensive.

Arizona's trouble generating pressure creates room for passing touchdowns to pile up. Minnesota presents the opposite problem, forcing hurried decisions against coverage that has punished opposing passers. And Washington can turn its quarterback loose against a Philadelphia defense struggling to finish the rush, making his legs an essential part of the offense.

Dak Prescott throws 5+ touchdown passes against the Cardinals

Arizona gives quarterbacks too much of everything: time, room downfield, and opportunities to finish drives. The Cardinals have surrendered 17 touchdown passes and allowed 8.5 yards per attempt, while their 31.8% pressure rate gives Prescott room to find the right matchup.

CeeDee Lamb commands attention; George Pickens supplies another scoring threat if his shoulder and hamstring permit his usual involvement. Javonte Williams can hold defenders near the line before Prescott throws behind them, turning balanced possessions into passing finishes. Prescott threw three touchdowns Monday. Against this coverage, Dallas keeps the scoring decisions in his hands – and five drives end with a touchdown pass.

Jared Goff throws 3+ interceptions against the Vikings

Goff brings 14 touchdown passes and zero interceptions into a matchup with Brian Flores. Minnesota brings a defense that has allowed three touchdown passes while collecting seven interceptions and generating pressure on 48.8% of opposing dropbacks. Goff can punish a blitz when he identifies the answer; Flores can make that answer arrive a fraction too late.

Detroit's line isn't suddenly broken – Cade Mays is off the injury report, and Penei Sewell's Wednesday absence was for rest – but Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs missing practice adds uncertainty around the quick outlets. Even if both play, Minnesota can crowd those answers and force contested throws. One disrupted route, one hurried release, and one forced attempt turn spotless ball security into a three-pick afternoon.

Jayden Daniels rushes for 125+ yards against the Eagles

Washington should make Daniels' legs a central part of Sunday night's offense. Terry McLaurin's season-ending injury narrows the passing menu, while Philadelphia ranks last in quick-pressure rate (8.9%) and sack rate (3.2%), giving Daniels opportunities to find escape lanes before the pocket collapses. Keepers can create rushing chances deliberately; scrambles can supply the explosives. Daniels ran for 103 yards against the Giants before the 49ers restricted him to 10, illustrating how much containment matters.

Philadelphia has uncertainty there: Jihaad Campbell missed Wednesday's practice, and several edge defenders were limited. Daniels practiced fully despite his left-elbow designation. With Laremy Tunsil still missing, Washington can move the launch point and attack space – until one broken containment assignment sends Daniels past 125.

articles.title: Mel Kiper Jr. Drops New Big Board with Arch Manning as QB6 for 2027 NFL Draft
articles.summary: Now two full months into the college football season, ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr. has released a new top-25 big board for the 2027 NFL draft.
articles.body:
Now two full months into the college football season, ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr. has released a new top-25 big board for the 2027 NFL draft.

Texas quarterback Arch Manning remains the sixth-best quarterback and No. 24 overall player for Kiper, who had him in those same spots in his previous ranking released on Oct. 15.

There is little surprise at the very top with Ohio State star Jeremiah Smith ranked No. 1 overall.

Report Card Grades for Top 20 College Football QBs 📝

Here's the updated top-10 list for Kiper with one month remaining in the college football regular season:

The other quarterbacks ahead of Manning on Kiper's big board are Drew Mestemaker, Darian Mensah, Trinidad Chambliss, CJ Carr and Austin Simmons.

Mestemaker's ascent to the top of the 2027 QB class is remarkable given he was unranked as a high-school prospect and spent his freshman year in college as the backup at North Texas.

Even if Manning wasn't ranked as the best quarterback prospect coming into the season, he was the one analysts frequently pointed to as being able to move into the top position if he played well because of his size, athleticism and raw ability.

Kiper cited those attributes as reasons Manning remains among his top-25 players, but also pointed out his "inconsistent" accuracy and decision-making as holding him back right now.

The turnovers are especially jarring for Manning. His seven interceptions in 196 pass attempts this season are as many as he had in 404 pass attempts in 2025.

Right behind Manning on Kiper's list is another quarterback thought to be in the mix for the No. 1 pick coming into the season: Oregon's Dante Moore.

Ducks head coach Dan Lanning announced on Monday that Moore is expected to miss the remainder of the season. He hasn't played since Sept. 26 after suffering a concussion on a late hit from USC linebacker Desman Stephens II.

The injury for Moore has led to questions about whether or not he will even enter the 2027 draft. He has one more year of college eligibility remaining, giving him the option of staying in school to rebuild his value and potentially be a top pick in 2028.

Moore would only be 23 when the 2028 NFL season starts if he did remain in college next year. For comparison, Trinidad Chambliss will be 25 at the start of the 2027 NFL season.

articles.title: Packers take big lead and then hold on over Panthers, who are suddenly in a slump
articles.summary: The Panthers and Packers were looking to bounce back from Week 7 losses.
articles.body: Through the Carolina Panthers' first five games, it looked like Bryce Young was having an impressive breakout. There were even MVP chants. Those chants, and the idea that the Panthers might be making a big leap as a team, need to be paused. In five days, the Panthers walked back most of the positive strides they collectively had made in recent weeks. They followed up an ugly 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday by being outplayed on both sides of the ball Thursday night against the Green Bay Packers in a 27-19 loss. It wasn't the blowout the Panthers suffered in Week 7 — the Panthers had a shot to tie in the final five minutes, but had a hapless drive and turned it over on downs — but they're 3-4 and not looking like a playoff contender lately. The Packers had a lot to do with the Panthers' issues. Green Bay's defense has looked much better lately and should get Micah Parsons back soon. The Packers' offensive line is playing much better than it was early in the season, Jordan Love is on a hot streak and Josh Jacobs has brought some balance to the offense. The Packers (5-3) could still be a factor in the NFC North. The Panthers should be a factor in the NFC South, but that's mostly because the division isn't very good. Carolina had some good vibes early in the season, and those have taken a big hit in less than a week. Packers overcome early miscuesThe Packers fumbled away the opening kickoff. They missed an extra point on a touchdown. Christian Watson lost another fumble. Matthew Golden dropped a pass in the end zone. It wasn't pretty. But they ended up OK. Watson caught a long pass, though he suffered a chest injury and went to the hospital as a precaution (and returned to the game in the second half). One play after dropping the touchdown, Golden caught a 24-yard score. The Packers' defense was tremendous in the first half. Or perhaps it was the Panthers' offense that was floundering, a week after it was terrible against the Buccaneers. There was too much pressure on Bryce Young, who rarely had a comfortable pass. He had just 65 yards at the half. Top receiver Tetairoa McMillan had one catch for 10 yards. Fellow starting receiver Jalen Coker didn't have a catch in the first two quarters. The Panthers had only 87 yards as a team.On the other side, Love had 189 yards and two touchdowns in the first half. The Packers led 20-10 at the half. Even though it was ugly at times, Green Bay looked good going into halftime.
